response_text: To set up multiple stacks using the same method from the lab, we just start with the initial MSP value and divide up the memory into equal-sized blocks for each thread. Each thread gets a fixed stack size, and we also leave space for the main stack. The starting address for thread j is found by adding the main stack size to the MSP value, then adding (j - 1) times the thread stack size. This way, each thread’s stack gets placed one after the other in memory, right after the main stack. We also need to make sure the stack sizes are multiples of 8 to stay aligned—otherwise the processor could crash. On top of that, we have to check that all the stack memory fits in RAM and doesn’t overlap with anything else. As long as we do all that, we can figure out safe and separate stack locations for every thread ahead of time.\n
